entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please say 'Returns' or 'New Order' to be routed to the correct department.
Returns.
Connecting you to a Returns Specialist now.
Thanks for calling VeloFit, my name is Alex. How can I help you today?
Hi Alex, I need to return a couple of items from a recent order. My order number is VF8675309.

I can certainly help with that. Let me pull up order VF8675309... Okay, I see it. You purchased the Velo-Pro Carbon shoes and a set of Velo-Grip all-weather tires, delivered 17 days ago. Is that correct?
Yes, that's the one. They just didn't work out for me, so I'd like to send them back for a refund.
No problem. You're well within the 90-day window. To process this, I just need to confirm the condition of the items. Are they still in new, unused condition with the original packaging?
Yeah, pretty much. I only tried them out for a short ride to see how they felt.
I understand. Can you clarify what 'tried them out' means? For the shoes, were cleats attached to them at any point?
Well, yes. I had to attach my cleats to clip into my bike. How else would I test them?
Okay, I appreciate the honesty. And the tires, were they put onto a wheelset?
Yes, I had them put on my bike for that same test ride.

I see. Unfortunately, I won't be able to accept these items for a return. Our policy is quite strict that items must be in resalable condition. Once cleats are **installed** on the shoes, it almost always leaves **cleat marks** on the carbon sole.

And for the tires, the moment they are **mounted** and ridden, even just around the block, they become used. We can't in good conscience sell someone else a set of **dirty tires** that have been on the road. I'm very sorry, but I have to deny the return based on their physical condition.
Are you kidding me? That's ridiculous! I spent over $300 on this gear. How am I supposed to know if I like it if I can't actually try it? This is a terrible policy.

I completely understand your frustration, and I agree it's a difficult situation. I really wish our policy had more flexibility for this. While I can't process a refund for the used items, I definitely want to help you out here. I can see you've been a loyal VeloFit customer for a while.
As a gesture of goodwill, I can offer you a $25 store credit. You could use it towards a different pair of shoes or another piece of gear.
Twenty-five dollars? That's it? That's kind of an insult after I just spent a fortune here. I expected better from VeloFit. This is making me rethink where I buy my gear.

You're right to be upset, and I sincerely apologize that this has been your experience. Your business is very important to us, and the last thing I want is for you to feel this way. Let me re-evaluate what I can do. Please hold for one moment.

Okay, thank you for your patience. Because you're a valued customer and to help make up for the policy inconvenience, I can increase that credit to $100. It's the absolute maximum I'm authorized for, but I think it's fair in this case. You can use it on any future purchase with us.
Wow, okay. $100 is... much better. That actually helps a lot. I guess I can just keep these as backups. That's a fair compromise.

I'm so glad we could find a solution for you. I've just applied the $100 credit to your VeloFit account. It's active right now and it will never expire. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
No, that's everything. Thank you, Alex. I really appreciate you working with me on this and finding a way to help.
It was my pleasure. Thank you for calling VeloFit, and have a great rest of your day.
